# ADR-1102: Detach Windows children with CREATE_NO_WINDOW and a breakaway decided from the measured job

## Status

accepted

## Context

Issue #684: five detached background spawns (`post_commit_reindex._spawn_reanalyze`, `session_lifecycle._spawn_consolidation`, `session_start._spawn_consolidate_cycle` and `_maybe_background_reanalyze`, `embedding_downloads._spawn_detached`) passed only `start_new_session=True`. CPython ignores that argument on Windows, so there the child kept the hook's console and process group. The capture drainer (ADR-1094) already used `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`, and the Codex plugin's `session_queue.spawn` had the same gap as the five.

A Windows job may terminate its processes when its last handle closes (`JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`). `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` takes a child out of the caller's job, but only if that job sets `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK`; in any other job `CreateProcess` fails, and outside a job the flag has no effect (Microsoft, process-creation-flags and JOBOBJECT_BASIC_LIMIT_INFORMATION). A reporter's local patch (Windows 11, 2026-10-07 to 10-13, 24 of 24 dream cycles completed) requested breakaway and retried without it on `OSError`. The same reporter measured a Python started by Claude Code through Git Bash: `IsProcessInJob` FALSE, `LimitFlags` 0x0. That was not measured inside a hook.

`DETACHED_PROCESS` gives the child no console, so each console program it starts gets a new, visible console window. `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` gives it a console without a window, which its console children share. The two cannot be combined (CREATE_NO_WINDOW is ignored with DETACHED_PROCESS).

## Decision

Every detached spawn takes its `Popen` options from `mcp_server.shared.detached_spawn.options()`. On POSIX it returns `start_new_session=True`. On win32 it returns `creationflags` only: `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, plus `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` when the caller runs in a job whose `LimitFlags` sets `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK` and not `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK` (with silent breakaway the child leaves without asking).

The job is measured before the spawn by `mcp_server.shared.win32_job.job_limit_flags()` (`IsProcessInJob` with a NULL job, then `QueryInformationJobObject` with `JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation`). The flags are decided once from that measurement; no spawn is retried with other flags. A failed measurement raises `OSError` at the spawn site, which logs it as a failed spawn. A job that allows no breakaway and kills on close keeps the child: the spawn proceeds without breakaway (the only flags `CreateProcess` accepts) and a WARNING says the child ends when the job closes.

This supersedes ADR-1094's `DETACHED_PROCESS` for the capture drainer. The stdlib-only Codex `session_queue.py` (ADR-1084), shipped without `mcp_server`, repeats the two constant flags, has no job probe, and a test keeps its values equal to `detached_spawn`'s.

## Consequences

The Windows branches are pure functions tested on every platform; the kernel32 calls are tested against a fake, and for real on the Windows CI leg. A detached child on Windows no longer shares the hook's console or process group, and leaves a job that lets it.

Each spawn on win32 costs two kernel32 calls. The real behaviour inside a Claude Code or Codex hook process on Windows remains unmeasured until a Windows run inside a hook reports it. A nested job is read at its immediate level only, as `QueryInformationJobObject` does. The Codex drain cannot leave a job that requires an explicit breakaway request.
